newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen up after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen up after jobs data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen moving higher on Friday after a report on March payrolls, wages and employment, analysts said.

The Labor Department said the economy added 175,000 new jobs in March and the jobless rate fell to 5.2 percent. Jobs growth in February was revised downward to show a 293,000 increase compared to 339,000 originally.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected 196,000 new jobs in the month and an unemployment rate of 5.2 percent.

Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities said, "The non-farm figure was friendly and they revised the previous one downward. But offsetting that is a rise in the hourly earnings. At the end of the day, nothing has changed. We came into today thinking the Fed will tighten on May 20, and these numbers don't change that. We'll be mixed to higher, only because this is out of the way. It's no longer staring us in the face."
